speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail, such as whether it consists of raised bumps, flat spots, or blisters? Also, have you noticed if the rash started on your face or trunk and then spread outwards?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression from a facial rash sparing the perioral area to the trunk and extremities, accompanied by mild prodromal symptoms, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). To confirm this, can you tell me if the rash on her cheeks had a distinct "slapped cheek" appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.
